body:
> This'll require some rewriting of the concept: as written, the spec today taints _the custom property itself_ if it's mentioned in a `@keyframes` rule, not the _value_ of a custom property that comes from an active animation. I don't know how browsers actually implement the tainting today, tho.

Blink indeed taints the _value_. (So e.g. `--x: 42 !important` would give a non-tainted computed value for `--x`, even a current animation on `--x` adds some effect value to the cascade.)

> This'll require some rewriting of the concept: as written, the spec today taints _the custom property itself_

That could make sense for separate reasons, but I don't think it's _required_ for this? I think this just means animation-taint information now only lives during the style resolution of a single element, and is never stored on the computed style in the first place (thus no taint to actively remove on inheritance)? Instead, `var()` etc would check the temporary taint info during substitution.
